## Defects found

**1. Mutable default argument (`seen=[]`)**
Default argument values are evaluated once, at function definition time, and the same list object is reused on every call that doesn't pass `seen` explicitly. Anything appended to it in one call is still there on the next call.
*Effect:* calling `top_scores(scores_a)` and later `top_scores(scores_b)` (both using the default) will cause values from `scores_a`'s run to "leak" into the dedup check for `scores_b`, silently dropping legitimate scores from `scores_b`'s result. Repeated calls become order-dependent and results shrink/change over the program's lifetime even though each call looks independent.

**2. `IndexError` when `limit` exceeds the length of `scores`**
The loop does `for i in range(0, limit): ... scores[i]` with no check that `i` stays within bounds of the (possibly shorter) list.
*Effect:* e.g. `top_scores([50, 20, 30])` with the default `limit=5` raises `IndexError: list index out of range` instead of returning the 3 available scores.

**3. Crash on empty `scores`**
If `scores == []`, the very first loop iteration does `scores[0]`, raising `IndexError` immediately (this is really a special case of #2, but worth calling out since an empty input is an easy, likely-to-occur case).

**4. Fixed loop range causes fewer than `limit` results when duplicates are present**
The loop only ever inspects the first `limit` positions of the sorted list (`range(0, limit)`); when a value at one of those positions is already in `seen` (e.g., a duplicate score), it is skipped but nothing later in the list is pulled in to replace it — the loop never extends past `limit`.
*Effect:* `top_scores([100, 100, 90, 80, 70, 60], limit=5)` sorts to `[100,100,90,80,70,60]` and returns only `[100, 90, 80, 70]` (4 items) even though a 5th distinct score (`60`) exists and should have been included to fill out the top 5.

**5. In-place mutation of the caller's list**
`scores.sort(reverse=True)` sorts the list the caller passed in, in place, rather than sorting a copy.
*Effect:* the caller's original list is silently reordered as a side effect of calling `top_scores`; any code elsewhere that relied on the original ordering of that same list object will see it changed after this call.
